# Creative contract

Read the current product, not just its landing-page headings. Record who it is
for, its core job, the action worth showing and the resulting state. Every
factual claim needs a local source and an exact supporting excerpt in the
profile. The agent still checks that the claim actually follows from that
evidence; substring matching is not a truth detector.

Write a short continuous introduction, explanation, payoff and closing
invitation. Avoid a chain of commands such as "Swipe. Vote. Click. Save."
Use canonical captions as the script source of truth. Spell out awkward
numbers/acronyms in pronunciation aliases when needed.

Use the project's own palette, font and logo. Reconstruct UI only when it
faithfully represents the real workflow, and label fictional demonstration
data. Original/cleared illustrations are preferable to copyrighted film art.

Plan readable holds before render. UI state tests belong to that product's
composition, not the generic toolkit. Test both forward and reverse seeking.
At each critical action check the destination, selection, counts, optional
score and confirmation independently.

The starter composition is not an artistic template to impose on every app.
Change its layout, scenes and rhythm for the product. Narration timing is
measured first; adapt motion and cuts to it without stretching finished audio.
Do not silently extend the requested duration to fit an overlong story.
